attention_paths.description: Pull requests changing files that match these glob patterns get a mark in the confirm popup.

dir.description: Where gh-triage keeps its clones and the worktrees Claude reads, and the lists last read (lists.json, shown at once at the next launch) (~ is your home); by default $XDG_CACHE_HOME/gh-triage, or ~/.cache/gh-triage.

approval.description: Checks that pass only after an approval, such as a policy bot's: glob patterns of check names. While only they are pending, CI shows ◌, and the checks count as passing when deciding a merge.

claude.description: C asks Claude Code (claude -p, with the account you are signed in with). On a pull request's screen, it reviews that pull request in a worktree of its head. On the list, it plans what to show and select in the tab shown, with no tools, and answers in the language you ask in; enter applies the plan, and an approve or a merge in it opens the confirm popup. Claude only reads: no settings files or MCP servers are loaded, its file tools see only the worktree, and it has none that run commands.

allowed_tools.description: The tools Claude may use, among "Read", "Grep", "Glob" and "WebFetch".

instructions.description: Appended to the instructions of every review and triage, such as "Point out changes that have no tests."

language.description: The language Claude answers in about a pull request, such as "Japanese". A review drafted with D is written in the language of the pull request instead.

model.description: The model Claude Code runs, as claude --model takes it.

release_notes_check.description: Let Claude read the release notes of the bot pull requests in the merge popup, and mark those that need care.

style.description: How a description is drawn, in the pane and on the PR screen: "rendered" (default) draws headings, lists, code, quotes and tables; "plain" shows the Markdown as written.

collapse.description: Files shown folded, as their name and line counts, until unfolded: glob patterns, matched against the base name unless they have a slash.

keys.description: Which keys do what, by action: a key or a list of keys, or [] to turn it off.

columns.description: The columns shown, in the order given; "pr" and "title" are needed. WHY shows on grouped tabs and the inbox only, and AUTHOR not on a tab of your own pull requests. On a narrow terminal SIZE goes first, then AUTHOR.

home_owners.description: Owners whose name is left out of the PR column, such as your company.

refresh.description: Refresh the shown tab this often, as a Go duration such as "3m" or "90s"; "off" refreshes only when R is pressed.

stale_days.description: Mark AGE when a pull request has not been updated for this many days, or "off".

level.description: How much goes to the log file: "debug", "info" (default), "warn" or "error". --debug and GH_TRIAGE_LOG_LEVEL take precedence. gh triage log prints where the file is.

auto_merge.description: Use GitHub's auto-merge where the repository allows it; elsewhere gh-triage waits for the checks and merges when they pass. Commits pushed after auto-merge is turned on are merged too, as GitHub does.

blocked_timeout.description: Where gh-triage waits, how long a pull request may stay blocked by another rule (a second approval, code owners) after its required checks finished. Only the time gh-triage is running counts.

checks_timeout.description: Where gh-triage waits, how long to wait for required checks still running. Only the time gh-triage is running counts.

methods.description: The order of preference among the methods a repository allows: "merge", "squash", "rebase". The first one the repository allows is used.

update_branch.description: Whose branch is updated when it is behind its base: "humans" (default), "all" or "never". Bots rebase their own branches, and some (renovate) stop updating a branch someone else committed to.

height.description: Lines of the preview pane under the list; 0 hides it until it is shown with a key. Dragging the pane's top edge, or + and -, changes them, and the lines set that way are kept over this one.

tab.description: The tab the pane opens on: "overview" (default), the description beside a column of facts, or "diff".

editor.description: The editor ctrl+e opens to write a review, with its arguments, such as "code --wait". Left out, $VISUAL, then $EDITOR.

mark_done.description: Mark a pull request's notification done after you review it here, from any tab.

bot.description: The author must be a bot.

max_files.description: The most files it may change.

name.description: The rule's name, as S lists it.

packages.description: The dependencies a renovate or dependabot pull request updates, read from its body; every one it updates must be listed.

title.description: A regular expression the title must match.

folded.description: The groups folded at start, among groups.

groups.description: The groups a search is split into, in the order shown.

kind.description: "search" (default), a GitHub search, or "inbox", the pull requests in your notifications.

limit.description: How many pull requests, or notifications, to read (at most 1000; 100 by default).

name.description: The tab's name; "inbox" for the inbox by default.

show_settled.description: The inbox shows notifications whose pull request is merged or closed from the start.

dark.description: The color scheme on a dark terminal, and on one that does not tell its background.

light.description: The color scheme on a light terminal. Write the same theme as theme.dark to use it on any terminal.
